subject: Pacing and liveness SLA proposal for streaming pilot - Acme Financial
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmefinancial.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: sre-team@acmefinancial.com
Date: 2026-02-18 09:12 -0500
Subject: Pilot SLA questions — streaming behavior

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're lining up a 6-week pilot to exercise the streaming endpoints for our customer assistant and have a couple of technical questions that will determine whether we can accept Redwood's default Hosted SLA or need a carve-out.

Specifically: 1) For streaming endpoints, can you confirm the typical time-to-first-token (TTFT) SLA you can guarantee for Hosted API (multi-tenant) vs Dedicated? Our compliance team is focused on TTFT because streaming is used in our UI. 2) For sustained conversation workloads, what are the realistic steady-state token/sec expectations per session and what burst support is available? 3) If TTFT occasionally exceeds the threshold during congestion, what automated fallback/rollback behavior do you recommend?

Attached is our short SLA questionnaire and sample traffic for next quarter. We're trying to map this to our procurement/Legal review this week.

Appreciate a concise answer we can share with security and procurement.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior SRE, Acme Financial
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-18 11:03 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — streaming behavior

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (solutions) and Marcus (runtime) so we can give both commercial and technical answers. Below is a short plan:

Action items (we'll own these):
- Marcus to provide concrete TTFT and tokens/sec profiles for Hosted vs Dedicated (by EOD).
- Vanessa to propose an operational fallback and monitoring playbook for the pilot.
- We'll return a single-sheet SLA addendum showing any carve-outs needed for the pilot.

High level answers up-front:
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): typical TTFT for streaming endpoints is 50–120 ms in non-congested regions; we target p95 < 250 ms under our standard SLA.
- Dedicated: with reserved GPU pools and pinned model variant we frequently observe TTFT < 30 ms p50 and p95 < 80 ms for the same prompt profile.
- Sustained tokens/sec: for Hosted endpoints we rate-limit per-customer session to avoid noisy neighbors — expect 8–12 tokens/s sustained, bursts to 20 tokens/s for short periods when capacity is available. Dedicated configurations can sustain 40–120 tokens/s depending on instance type (we'll include a recommended sizing table).

We'll confirm exact numbers for your sample traffic and propose a formal SLA note. Is procurement comfortable with an initial pilot carve-out (time-boxed) while we validate metrics?

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-18 14:26 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — streaming behavior

Stephanie / Vanessa — following up with the detailed runtime notes for Acme's pilot. I kept this targeted so Legal/Security can pick what they need.

1) Measurement definition (important): when we say TTFT (time-to-first-token) we measure from request received at the edge to first non-empty token byte emitted to the client (includes auth + routing). For streaming via our HTTPS chunked responses / SSE we instrument at env edge and at the inference worker to provide both edge-to-first-byte and worker-queue-wait metrics.

2) Typical numbers (observed under our internal benchmarks using your prompt mix):
- Hosted multi-tenant (standard routing): p50 ~ 60 ms, p90 ~ 140 ms, p95 ~ 240 ms under typical 95th percentile load. In congestion windows (regional spikes) p95 can degrade toward 400–600 ms temporarily if autoscaling tail latency reacts.
- Dedicated (1x A100-class pool, pinned model): p50 ~ 20–25 ms, p90 ~ 55–80 ms, p95 ~ 90–120 ms. Dedicated reduces queuing variability and KV cache warmup is faster.

3) Tokens/sec assumptions & sizing:
- Hosted default safety: we enforce per-session soft caps to preserve multi-tenant fairness — sustained 8–12 t/s, 20 t/s short bursts.
- Dedicated sizing: a single 8-GPU pool tailored to your model variant should handle sustained 60–80 t/s across 200 concurrent sessions for your predicted prompt sizes. We'll provide a recommended pool sizing matrix (GPU type vs expected t/s).

4) Fallback & graceful degradation patterns we recommend for pilot (what we can commit to operationally):
- Canary routing: during pilot hours route a percentage (10–20%) of requests to Dedicated if available, otherwise to Hosted.
- Time-based fallback: for any request crossing TTFT threshold > configured SLA during pilot, we return a diagnostic header (X-Redwood-Fallback: queued) and kick the client to a non-streaming synchronous endpoint (single-response) as a fallback. This results in complete output but may increase perceived latency; we document both paths in the addendum.
- Alerting: integration to your PagerDuty + our console tracing; automatic ticket creation for p95 TTFT breaches for 5+ minutes.

5) Compensation and exceptions: for the pilot we can include an SLA note that allows a narrow carve-out for 3 short congestion windows per month (duration and remediation steps defined). For production you'd need a Dedicated commitment for stricter TTFT guarantees.

I'll attach a short CSV of the bench runs against your sample traffic (attached). Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through numbers.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — circling back with the concrete numbers and operational plan (Marcus attached the bench CSV and Vanessa will follow-up with the playbook). Short summary you can share with Procurement / Security:

- TTFT expectations (pilot carve-out): Hosted p95 target 250 ms, Dedicated p95 target 120 ms.
- Sustained tokens/sec (pilot baseline): Hosted 8–12 t/s sustained with 20 t/s short bursts; Dedicated recommended 60–80 t/s sustained for the pilot sizing we propose.
- Fallback behavior: automatic diagnostic headers + synchronous non-stream fallback if TTFT threshold is breached. We will instrument and export the TTFT metric to your monitoring and create automated alerts when p95 > threshold for 5 minutes.
- Commercial ask: a 3-month pilot carve-out addendum that limits punitive credits for up to 3 regional congestion events (we'll enumerate remediations). Post-pilot, Dedicated commitments provide stricter TTFT SLAs.

Next steps: 1) Vanessa to propose the SLA addendum + monitoring runbook, 2) Procurement to confirm whether the limited carve-out is acceptable, 3) Schedule a short runbook review (30 minutes) next week to sign off.

If you give the green light we'll send the formal addendum and proposed dates.

Best — Stephanie
